weather.text: A broad market with volatility around normal; family broadening carry, a partial fit, at 1.00x the PM's own risk (a reading, not a size). Oldest input 13 Nov, the Friday close.
RISK OFF, trend regime DOWNTREND; the handbook's doctrine is that breadth is against the tape, so build the watchlist and do not push new entries. A reading, not an Aegis rule.
Light RED: SPY 754.37 sits 0.68% under the 759.51 flip, with the put wall at 750 and the call wall at 775, so dealers amplify moves until SPY is back over the flip.
Breadth says the average stock still keeps up but the phase is late; trend and dealer positioning say breakouts get sold, and the one ADVANCE still waits on volume.

weather.stance: Read: Valen's stance is RISK OFF against NEUTRAL a month ago (no record five days ago), and the trend regime is DOWNTREND now, five days ago and a month ago. SPY and QQQ have neither a daily nor a weekly buy signal and neither sits above a rising 5-day line; SPY is 0.91 daily ranges under its 50-day and QQQ 2.32, and VIX/VIX3M is 0.94 (1.04 five days ago), neither calm nor stressed. Handbook doctrine, not an Aegis rule: breadth is against the tape, build the watchlist, do not push new entries.
weather.gex: Read: the light is RED. SPY at 754.37 sits 0.68% under the 759.51 flip, with the put wall at 750 (0.58% below) and the call wall at 775 (2.73% above), so dealers amplify moves both ways; reclaiming the flip calms the tape and losing 750 removes the cushion. QQQ is 1.73% under its 691.68 flip and sitting on its 680 put wall, call wall 700. Dealer side is the standard assumption, not observed data.
weather.heartbeat: Read: the average stock has kept up with the index for 20 days (broadening): +4.52% over 20 days and +1.50% over 60, but -0.22% over the last 5, with confidence 0.75 and a place at the top of its 12-month range, so the phase is late rather than early. The ratio is 1.72% above its 20-day average (0.2881) and 1.92% under its 12-month high; a cross under that average would turn it before the label changes.
weather.positioning: Read: trend funds are neutral across 18 markets with none at an extreme (dial 1.00), leaning long currencies (+0.57) and short rates (-0.44) and metals (-0.36). Nearest lines: they turn buyers of natural gas above 3.16 (0.03% away) and sellers of soybeans below 1,225.44 (0.15% below); for stocks, they turn sellers of the S&P 500 below 7,492.29 (1.2% below) and of the Russell 2000 below 2,744.43 (1.71% below), and buyers of the Nasdaq 100 above 28,333.58 (1.47% above).
weather.volatility: Read: VIX at 19.3 is higher than 74% of days in two years, so the index is not quiet; VIX/VIX3M is 0.94, down from 1.04 five days ago and under the 1.00 stress line, and the curve is in contango. Single stocks imply 42.77, a gap of 23.47 that is wider than 78% of the past two years and has widened 1.75 points in 20 days, now 1.25% under the elevated band at 23.76; implied correlation is 11.8.
weather.divergence: Read: one market-level warning is lit, price climbing while momentum falls, and Valen counts 1 of 8 types fired; Crown counts a further 5 on individual markets, 6 lit in all. No single one is a reason to sell: they matter when several agree with breadth, and breadth is still broadening.
weather.call: Read: Crown's family is broadening carry, a partial fit at a 1.00x multiplier on the PM's own risk (a reading, not a size): breadth broadening, the stock-level gap normal and trend funds near a low flip are met, while breadth not at an extreme and dealers long gamma both fail. The leading macro story is a dollar squeeze with 76.16% of its conditions met at full coverage, not contested, runner-up inflation shock. Next tests: retail sales 17 Nov 08:30 ET, FOMC 18 Nov 14:00 ET, jobless claims 19 Nov, ISM 23 Nov, core PCE 25 Nov.
weather.cot: Read: big speculators are crowded long the Nasdaq 100, small caps (Russell 2000), the 30-year bond and the 5- and 2-year notes, and crowded short crude oil, natural gas and silver. The equity crowding (Nasdaq 100 and small caps) is the one that matters for a stock book, as context and not timing; the report covers 3 Nov.
weather.checklist: Read: net new highs lead (8-day average 69.0 against 46.8 over 20 days), but today's count is not green, the 5-day up/down 4% count is 0.72 against the 1.00 pass, the 10-day count is 0.70 and monthly big risers are 67. Above their 20-day line 48.2%, 50-day 45.9%, 200-day 54.0% and 40-day 47.6%: a market with fewer than half its stocks above the medium lines, with these counts labelled by the file as US-listed stocks over $2B, not AQE's own list.
weather.turning: Read: stance RISK OFF now against NEUTRAL a month ago (no record five days ago); trend DOWNTREND throughout; VIX/VIX3M 0.94 against 1.04 and 0.89; stocks above their 40-day line 47.6% against 42.0% a month ago; SPY -0.91 daily ranges from its 50-day against -2.89 and +0.48. Stocks above their 40-day line clearing 50 or the 5-day count clearing 1.00 (now 0.72) would turn it positive, the 5-day count under 0.70 negative, and the 350 monthly-risers line is a whole-market count (now 67), not a target on AQE's list.
weather.themes: Read: Valen lists Semiconductors, Chip Equipment, Social Media, Oil Services and Infra Power as real leadership, but they are +8.72%, +8.16%, +7.49%, +6.72% and +6.6% on the week against -8.32%, -6.24%, -4.29%, -3.93% and -9.09% on the month and sit 34%, 44%, 31%, 27% and 28% under their highs: violent turns in broken groups, not leaders. True leaders near their highs are Insurance (0.95% under), REITs (3.34%) and E-Commerce (4.07%); Infra Construction, Cloud Computing, Cybersecurity, Agri Commodities and Defense Tech are bounces off the floor.
weather.groups: Read: the turning sectors are Communication Services (LFTO, LBTYK, LION), Technology (APP, PCOR, FROG) and Energy (RRC, VVV, CRK); the turning themes with two or more strong names are Enterprise Software (U, BOX, ZM), Gaming Streaming (U, SIRI, SPOT), AI Software (APP, SAIL), Social Media (APP, TTD), AI Infrastructure (ANET, CCI), Infra Construction (CSX, MDU), Mag7 (TSLA, AAPL) and Big Banks (RF, JPM). plan: Before 21:30 SGT: Crown's calendar lists no US release today; retail sales print 17 Nov at 08:30 ET and the FOMC decides 18 Nov at 14:00 ET, and the book holds under its two broker stops.
At the open (22:30 SGT): read SPY (754.37) against the 759.51 flip (0.68% above) and the 750 put wall (0.58% below); a hold above the flip calms the tape, a break of 750 removes the cushion.
